checks: Verified source 6c56e9569b9982d7 §§2 and 4, (5)–(6) and (12), and its byte digest. The frozen proof replaces the original midpoint-equality route by the accepted cap cover.

Joint cap continuity and compactness give an actual maximizing mark of K. Monotonicity at that mark gives A(K)≤D_L(g)≤A(L), so putative equality forces g to maximize in L, as needed by the cover theorem.

In each active L cap the K trace has volume at least D_K(g)=A(K) and at most A(L). Both volumes are then equal and positive. For proper inclusion of positive compact convex traces, an exterior point of the larger trace has positive distance from the smaller closed trace; interpolation slightly toward an interior point gives an exterior interior point and a ball in the difference.

The active halfspaces are actual and cover the ambient continuous space, so the equal trace identities union to K=L. No full-rank assumption on the normals is needed. In dimension one the selected normals are opposite and the two half-lines cover the line.

dependencies.mapping: Set n=1, P={0} and K_0 equal to the body in question. The family is compatible because conv({0}×B)={0}×B and total mass is positive. For a nonzero continuous normal the base term vanishes identically, so c_0(u,u·g) is exactly the ordinary cap volume; pure-base containing cuts capture the whole body and cannot lower the minimum. The actual deepest mark therefore meets the hypotheses. The finite active collection has positive coefficients summing its normals to zero, and its ordinary closed traces cover the plane, including in d=1. Use B=L at the common maximizing mark, and restrict the cover from {0}×R^d to R^d.

overlap.comparison: Supplies an active cover for one compatible family at a maximizing mark. It does not compare the maxima of a properly nested pair; the frozen proof transfers the cover using an assumed common value and strict volume monotonicity.

readability: The positive-volume assertion uses an inball at any interior mark of K to give A(K)>0; it does not require a separate uniqueness theorem.

summary: A proper containing ordinary convex body has strictly larger maximal raw depth; equality would force every cap trace in a finite covering family to agree.
